chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

“wudu (ablution) is only a limit from the limits of Allah, so that Allah may know who obeys Him and who disobeys Him. And indeed, nothing renders the believer impure; rather, what suffices him is something like oil.”

key_terms.الدَّهْنِ: oil; used here as a comparison for a light application
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer, understood here as not becoming intrinsically impure
key_terms.حَدٌّ: a fixed limit or boundary set by divine law
key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the divinely established limits and ordinances of Allah
key_terms.يَعْصِيهِ: disobeys Him, by violating the divine command
key_terms.يُطِيعُهُ: obeys Him, by complying with the divine command

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام describe wudu (ablution) as a boundary from the limits of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith presents wudu (ablution) as a divinely ordained boundary through which obedience and disobedience are distinguished. It also indicates that the believer is not intrinsically defiled by impurity, and that a light application of water, like oiling, is sufficient in the context being described.
